headline: Cisco and Nvidia showed a new plug-in optical network part meant to move far more data between chips in AI data centers.
score_reason: Lowered from 6: the announcement is from the 12-13 Oct summit, a few days old; performance figures are Cisco's own.
importance_line: It could ease the network limits of giant AI clusters and cut costs if rivals adopt the standard, but the figures are the companies' claims and products are not yet proven.
summary: SiliconANGLE reports, in a column by analyst Zeus Kerravala of ZK Research, that Cisco unveiled with Nvidia a new plug-in optical module, called USFP, at the Open Compute Project summit, which Cisco says is the first of its kind to handle 400 gigabits per lane and carries about four times the data per size of today's leading modules. Cisco is also working with TE Connectivity and Amphenol to make it an industry standard, which the analyst argues could bring more suppliers and lower prices; these figures come from Cisco.
notes: Original TechSpot page blocked; read SiliconANGLE column instead (guest analyst view). Announcement date approximate (OCP summit week, column dated 13 Oct).
